api/api/GameFramework.Config.Enums.Confi.summary: Enum ConfigFlags Behavioral flags that control how configuration variables are handled Can be combined using bitwise OR to give variables multiple behaviors Usage Examples: Flags.Save: Variable persists between sessions Flags.Save | Flags.ServerInfo: Variable persists AND is sent to clients Flags.Cheat: Variable can only be modified when cheats are enabled Namespace: GameFramework.Config.Enums Assembly: .dll Syntax [Flags] public enum ConfigFlags Fields Name Description Cheat Variable is considered a cheat and can only be modified when cheats are enabled Used for debug variables, god mode, infinite resources, etc. Provides protection against accidental or unauthorized modifications ClientInfo Variable is sent from client to server when connecting or when value changes Used for client preferences that server needs to know: preferred name, color, etc. Allows server to customize experience based on client preferences None Default behavior - temporary variable, not saved or replicated Save Variable should be saved to configuration file and loaded on startup Used for user preferences, graphics settings, key bindings, etc. Triggers file I/O operations when modified ServerInfo Variable is sent from server to clients when they connect or when value changes Used for server settings that affect gameplay: time limits, player counts, etc. Ensures all clients have consistent server configuration User Variable was created dynamically by user (not predefined in code) Used for custom variables created through console or scripting May have different validation or cleanup behavior

api/api/GameFramework.Core.DiContainer.h.title: Class DiContainer | UCTools Base Project
api/api/GameFramework.Core.DiContainer.h.summary: Class DiContainer Enhanced dependency injection container with automatic constructor injection support. Supports singleton registration, factory registration, type bindings, and automatic dependency resolution. Inheritance object DiContainer Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: GameFramework.Core Assembly: .dll Syntax public class DiContainer Remarks This DI container provides three main registration patterns: Singleton: One instance created and reused for all requests Transient: New instance created for each request Factory: Custom factory function called for each request The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies using reflection, selecting the constructor with the most parameters and recursively resolving all dependencies. Circular dependency detection prevents infinite resolution loops. Design Benefits: Clean separation of concerns, automatic dependency resolution, easy testing, loose coupling Trade-offs: Runtime dependency resolution, potential circular dependencies, reflection overhead Examples // Register services container.RegisterSingleton<ILogger, ConsoleLogger>(); container.RegisterTransient<IRepository, DatabaseRepository>(); container.RegisterFactory<IConnection>(() => new SqlConnection(connectionString)); // Resolve services (automatic constructor injection) var service = container.Resolve<IMyService>(); Properties Instance Gets the singleton instance of the DI container. Declaration public static DiContainer Instance { get; } Property Value Type Description DiContainer The singleton DIContainer instance. Remarks Creates a new instance on first access. The container is designed to be used as a singleton to maintain consistent service registrations across the application. Methods Clear() Clears all registrations from the container. Declaration public void Clear() Remarks This method removes all singleton instances, factories, type bindings, and clears the resolution stack. Primarily useful for testing scenarios where you need to reset the container state between tests. IsRegistered(Type) Checks if a service type is registered in the container. Declaration public bool IsRegistered(Type type) Parameters Type Name Description Type type The service type to check. Returns Type Description bool True if the type is registered; otherwise, false. Remarks Checks all registration types: singleton instances, factories, and type bindings. IsRegistered<T>() Checks if a service type T is registered in the container. Declaration public bool IsRegistered<T>() Returns Type Description bool True if the type is registered; otherwise, false. Type Parameters Name Description T The service type to check. Remarks Use this method to conditionally resolve services or verify registrations during testing and debugging. Examples if (container.IsRegistered<IOptionalService>()) { var service = container.Resolve<IOptionalService>(); service.DoSomething(); } RegisterFactory<T>(Func<T>) Registers a factory function that creates new instances on each resolution request. Declaration public void RegisterFactory<T>(Func<T> factory) where T : class Parameters Type Name Description Func<T> factory The factory function that creates instances of T. Type Parameters Name Description T The service type to register. Remarks Use factory registration when you need custom creation logic, configuration, or when each request should receive a fresh instance with specific setup. The factory function is called every time the service is resolved. Examples container.RegisterFactory<IDatabase>(() => new SqlDatabase(GetConnectionString())); container.RegisterFactory<IHttpClient>(() => new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) }); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentNullException Thrown when factory is null. RegisterSingleton<T>() Registers a singleton for a concrete type (no interface mapping). Declaration public void RegisterSingleton<T>() where T : class Type Parameters Name Description T The concrete type to register as singleton. Remarks Convenience method for registering concrete types as singletons when no interface abstraction is needed. Examples container.RegisterSingleton<GameManager>(); RegisterSingleton<T>(T) Registers a pre-created singleton instance that will be returned for all requests of type T. Declaration public void RegisterSingleton<T>(T instance) where T : class Parameters Type Name Description T instance The singleton instance to register. Type Parameters Name Description T The service type to register. Remarks Use this method when you have a pre-configured instance that should be shared across the entire application. The instance will not be recreated. Examples var logger = new FileLogger("/logs/app.log"); container.RegisterSingleton<ILogger>(logger); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentNullException Thrown when instance is null. RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>() Registers a singleton mapping from interface to implementation type. The instance will be created on first request using constructor injection. Declaration public void RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>() where TImplementation : class, TInterface Type Parameters Name Description TInterface The service interface type. TImplementation The concrete implementation type. Remarks The implementation instance is created lazily on first request and then cached for all subsequent requests. Constructor dependencies are automatically resolved. Examples container.RegisterSingleton<IUserService, DatabaseUserService>(); // First call creates instance, subsequent calls return cached instance var service1 = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); var service2 = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); // Same instance as service1 RegisterTransient<TInterface, TImplementation>() Registers a transient type binding where a new instance is created for each request. Declaration public void RegisterTransient<TInterface, TImplementation>() where TImplementation : class, TInterface Type Parameters Name Description TInterface The service interface type. TImplementation The concrete implementation type. Remarks Transient services create a new instance every time they are requested. Use this for stateless services or when you need isolated instances. Constructor dependencies are automatically resolved for each new instance. Examples container.RegisterTransient<IEmailService, SmtpEmailService>(); // Each resolution creates a new instance var email1 = container.Resolve<IEmailService>(); var email2 = container.Resolve<IEmailService>(); // Different instance than email1 Resolve<T>() Resolves a service instance of type T using automatic constructor injection. Declaration public T Resolve<T>() where T : class Returns Type Description T An instance of type T with all dependencies injected. Type Parameters Name Description T The service type to resolve. Remarks This is the primary method for retrieving services from the container. The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies recursively. Resolution order: singleton instances → factories → type bindings → direct creation. Examples // Assuming UserService has constructor: UserService(ILogger logger, IDatabase db) var userService = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); // Logger and Database are automatically injected Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Thrown when the service is not registered and cannot be created directly, or when a circular dependency is detected.

api/api/GameFramework.Core.GameContext.h.summary: Class GameContext Centralized context object that provides access to all core game services through dependency injection. This class serves as a service aggregator that collects all essential game systems into a single, easily injectable dependency for game states and other complex systems. Inheritance object GameContext Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: GameFramework.Core Assembly: .dll Syntax public class GameContext Remarks The GameContext follows the Context Object pattern, providing a clean way to pass multiple related services to classes that need access to various game systems. Rather than injecting each service individually, classes can inject the GameContext and access all services through it. Benefits: Reduces constructor parameter count in dependent classes Provides a stable interface even when service dependencies change Centralizes service access for easier testing and mocking Maintains clear dependency relationships through constructor injection All services are validated for null values during construction, ensuring that the GameContext is always in a valid state when successfully created. Examples // In a game state constructor public class PlayingState : IGameState { private readonly GameContext _context; public PlayingState(GameContext context) { _context = context; } public void Enter() { _context.AudioService.PlayMusic("gameplay"); _context.UIService.ShowScreen("hud"); _context.EventSystem.Publish(new GameStartedEvent()); } } Constructors GameContext(IEventSystem, ISceneService, IAudioService, IInputManager, IUIService, ISaveService, IGameDataService, IConsoleService, IGraphicsService, IPauseService, ITimeService, IInstantiationService) Initializes a new instance of the GameContext with all required game services. Declaration public GameContext(IEventSystem eventSystem, ISceneService sceneService, IAudioService audioService, IInputManager inputManager, IUIService uiService, ISaveService saveService, IGameDataService gameDataService, IConsoleService consoleService, IGraphicsService graphicsService, IPauseService pauseService, ITimeService timeService, IInstantiationService instantiationService) Parameters Type Name Description IEventSystem eventSystem The event system for game event management. ISaveService saveService The save service for game data persistence. IGameDataService gameDataService The game data service for runtime game state. IConsoleService consoleService IGraphicsService graphicsService IPauseService pauseService ITimeService timeService IInstantiationService instantiationService Remarks This constructor uses dependency injection to receive all core game services. All parameters are validated for null values, ensuring that the GameContext is always created in a valid state with all required dependencies. The constructor is designed to be called by the dependency injection container during application startup. Manual instantiation is not recommended as it requires managing all service dependencies manually. Examples // Typically handled by DI container container.RegisterSingleton<GameContext>(); // Container automatically provides all dependencies var context = container.Resolve<GameContext>(); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentNullException Thrown when any of the required service parameters is null. api/api/GameFramework.Services.html.title: Namespace GameFramework.Services | UCTools Base Project
api/api/GameFramework.Services.html.summary: Namespace GameFramework.Services Classes AudioService AudioService with intelligent music management Compares requested clips against currently playing clips to avoid unnecessary restarts INTENT: Centralize all audio intelligence in the service layer DESIGN: Compare actual AudioClips rather than relying on external state checks PROS: Clean separation of concerns, states stay simple, centralized audio logic CONS: Requires clip comparison overhead (minimal) ConsoleService Service that orchestrates the debug console system using dependency injection. Now integrates with debug settings for console and logging control. Architecture: Manages console state (open/closed) based on debug.console_enabled setting Manages verbose logging based on debug.verbose_logging setting Provides public API for other systems to interact with console Input conflict management is handled by ConsoleInputHandler Flow: Receives toggle input events from InputManager Checks if console is enabled in debug settings Updates console open/closed state only if enabled Applies logging settings when configuration changes ConsoleInputHandler automatically manages input conflicts by checking IsConsoleOpen() GameDataService Central service for managing current game data (GameSessionData and PlayerData) Provides controlled access to game state and integrates with save system Uses EventSystem for change notifications and automatic save system registration GraphicsService Graphics service that handles all Unity graphics API calls Responds to configuration changes via events INTENT: Centralize all graphics settings application DESIGN: Event-driven graphics management, single responsibility PROS: Clean separation, all graphics logic in one place, easily testable CONS: Additional service complexity InstantiationService Service responsible for instantiating game objects, particularly the player prefab. Integrates with the event system to notify about instantiation events. Works with GameDataService to configure PlayerData components from save data. NotificationService Service that manages notification popups and automatically subscribes to game events to display contextual notifications to the player PauseService Simple centralized pause service that manages game pause state Handles time scale, audio, and event integration Uses EventSystem for all event publishing instead of local events ProfilingService Simplified profiling service that monitors performance metrics and manages frame-based profiling sessions. Design: Frame-based profiling with simple progress tracking Circular buffers for efficient memory management Event-driven architecture for UI updates Direct Unity Profiler integration for accurate metrics Pros: Clean separation of concerns Efficient memory usage Simple session management Comprehensive performance monitoring Cons: Memory overhead for data storage Dependency on EventSystem Performance impact during sessions SceneService Scene service implementation with constructor injection and progress reporting support TimeService TimeService manages game time tracking by directly updating GameSessionData GameSessionData is the single source of truth for game time Uses double precision internally for accurate tracking of large time values UIService UI service implementation with constructor injection and centralized screen updates Implements IUpdatable to manage frame-based updates for screens that need them Now handles debug settings integration for automatic debug popup management Structs PerformanceSnapshot Single performance data point captured at a specific moment
